question: Were tasks, reference answers and tests checked for errors that reject a correct solution?
checked_means: coverage, findings and limits of the check reported

applicability.reason: B05 applies always; the tests of these tasks decide which patches count as resolved.

check.procedure: Sources report: OpenAI annotators screened FAIL_TO_PASS tests of 1,699 samples (3 annotators each), and in 2026 six engineers audited 138 Verified problems. Study records (made by the study harness, not by this rater): each of the pilot and 20 source tasks was run with the code before the fix (every FAIL_TO_PASS test fails) and with the real fix (all tests pass); all 21 are marked eligible. A further record (made by another Claude run) grades a patch that fixes only the issue text of sympy__sympy-18199 and finds it rejected. The rater read these records and the sources and did not run code.
check.detection_limits: The check could not detect correct solutions that the tests reject for tasks other than sympy__sympy-18199 where no alternative patch was run, and the eligibility runs only show that the reference fix passes, not that other correct fixes do.

evidence.quote: We annotated 1,699 random samples from the SWE-bench test set
each sample is labeled 3 times by separate annotators
Whether the FAIL_TO_PASS unit tests filter out valid solutions.
at least 59.4% of the audited problems have flawed test cases that reject functionally correct submissions
We conducted an audit of 138 SWE-bench Verified problems
An example of too wide test cases is sympy__sympy-18199

reasons: The sources report a test review with its coverage (1,699 samples, three annotators each; later 138 problems, six engineers each), findings and limits, so Documented is passed. The result is outcome failed, not Contradicted: the 2026 audit is itself a reported check that found flawed tests in a subset of the audited problems, and for this scope it names only sympy__sympy-18199, which is listed as a task defect. The level is not lowered by the later audit; the findings are added to the detection limits.
missing: A reported check of these 21 tasks with alternative correct patches, which would show whether the other tasks reject correct solutions; a person review of the 18199 minimal patch, since the record itself says it does not show that the patch is a complete fix.
checks_performed: Read the 2024 and 2026 OpenAI posts for the procedure, coverage and findings of the test review
Read the eligibility records of the pilot and the 20 source tasks (all eligible)
Read the protocol 4 counterexample record for sympy__sympy-18199 and the issue text

task_defects.summary: The only FAIL_TO_PASS test, test_solve_modular, rejects a patch that implements the root 0 for a % p == 0 described in the issue; it fails on assertions about composite moduli, which the issue does not mention. The full reference patch passes. The record does not claim the minimal patch is a complete fix.
task_defects.quote: Then x = 0 mod p is also a root of this equation.

instructions: Record evidence locations with short quotes, the check performed, its outcome, detection limits, and reasons. The check outcome is the result of the check described in the procedure; state whether the benchmark sources report it or the auditor performed it. A rating without evidence and reasons is incomplete. Missing evidence is not a defect; a defect needs a cited location, and an oracle defect needs an executed counterexample.
